thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: p99 tail latency spike detected on cont-batching path for streaming routes (service=runtime, route=/v1/chat/stream). p95 ~350ms -> 600ms, p99 ~1.8s -> 6.2s. paging on-call: @sara

sara: on it. seeing alerts in grafana. ETA 5m to triage, paging infra/serving.

elena: I can pull traces, looks like a lot of stalled write loops around kv-cache renewals. streaming clients stuck in 'sending' state for some requests. :eyes:

jamie: I grabbed the k8s events — a few nodes had OOM killers but not many. scheduler logs show imbalanced batch distribution: some workers got large mixed-seqlen batches and stuck longer.

rahul: quick question — is this only cont-batching or also adaptive xla path?

elena: primarily cont-batching. adaptive/fastpath p99 unchanged. confirms it's the continuous batching queue.

ops-bot: running quick mitigation playbook: set `runtime.cont_batch.enabled=false` for prod cluster-alpha.

sara: hold on before flipping globally — want to try soft mitigations first: 1) reduce `cont_batch.max_batch_size` from 64 -> 32 2) enable `fair_sharing=true` to avoid head-of-line large batches 3) bump `streaming.write_timeout_ms` from 3000 -> 7000? (to avoid client disconnects)

jamie: agree. reducing max_batch_size should help tail without killing throughput. doing `kubectl patch` on configmap now for alpha. I'll post commands.

jamie: ```
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap runtime-config --type=json -p='[ {"op":"replace","path":"/data/cont_batch.max_batch_size","value":"32"}, {"op":"replace","path":"/data/cont_batch.fair_sharing","value":"true"} ]'
```

ops-bot: configmap patch applied to alpha; applying to canary nodes only first.

linda: rolling canary to 3 pods with new config. watch logs for increased small-batch count.

elena: traces from canary show p99 drop from ~6s -> ~2.1s on those pods. streaming stalls reduced.

rahul: nice. still seeing a subset with 4-5s spikes — probably machines that kept old kernel scheduling?

jamie: I'm going to toggle the scheduler fairness knob on the shard-level overlay so long-running batches yield sooner. command:
```sh
curl -XPOST "http://scheduler-api/shards/overlay/alpha/fair_share" -d '{"enabled": true, "preempt_ms": 50}'
```

ops-bot: scheduler overlay updated.

sara: monitoring prod traffic now. p95 looks back to ~330ms, p99 ~1.9s — better but still above target of 1.2s. streaming error count decreased 80%.

elena: we should also consider temporarily routing new streaming requests to the non-cont batching variant (fallback model) for critical tenants. Can we add a route rule?

jamie: yes — adding a policy in router: `if route==/v1/chat/stream and tenant in (critical-list) => model_variant=stream-noncont`

jamie: ```
# router-api
POST /v1/policies
{ "name": "stream-fallback-critical", "match": {"path": "/v1/chat/stream", "tenant_group": "critical"}, "action": {"model_variant":"stream-noncont"}}
```

ops-bot: policy created and applied. affected tenants: acme-inc, example-fin, beta-shop.

sara: customer-impact check: oncall page shows 12 tenants had degraded p99 >3s. only 2 active incident customer reports so far (acme-inc experiencing streaming stalls). I pinged their CSM.

linda: acme on Slack reported session timeouts ~10:12 UTC, we applied fallback for them at 10:24 and they report partial improvement.

rahul: to be safe, starting a controlled rollback plan: if p99 doesn't return under 1.5s in next 20m, flip `cont_batch.enabled=false` globally and schedule a maintenance window to analyze.

sara: agreed. starting 20m timer. passing to jamie for overnight handoff if spike regresses.

(elapsed ~12m)

elena: quick note — there are a few requests with mixed-seqlen > 8x difference causing huge KV cache miss churn, contributing to long tail. We should add request-size bucketing metric to differentiate.

jamie: logging that as follow-up: add `request.seq_len_ratio` histogram and alert if > 8 for more than 1% of batches.

linda: customer comms: draft message for CSM team: "We've identified continuous-batching contention causing intermittent streaming stalls for high-mix sequence workloads. We've applied routing fallbacks for critical tenants and reduced batch sizes; degradation is improving. We'll follow up with root cause and permanent fix."

sara: nice. I'll post to #incidents and set priority to P2 for now.

ops-bot: 20m timer expired, p99 steady at ~1.6s, p95 ~320ms.

jamie: handing off to night oncall @jamie — I'll keep monitoring alerts and follow up in AM with root-cause work items: 1) sched fairness tune 2) cont-batch algorithm guardrail for mixed seqlen 3) metric + alert 4) regression test in staging using mixed sequence replay.

sara: thanks team. action items assigned: jamie (follow-up fixes + rollout), elena (traces + replay harness), rahul (postmortem draft), linda (customer comms). I'll close thread once postmortem link posted. :thumbsup:

jamie: quick add — suggest we add a temporary canary that disables cont-batching for streaming only during peak hours as a later mitigation option.

elena: noted. creating ticket: INC-2026-contbatch-tail-2026 in backlog.
